problem_statement:
When a profile, saved-verse, or reflection write cannot be sent, keep it and replay it in order.

One pending profile patch. A later profile patch replaces the earlier one.
One pending save or unsave per verse reference. A later one replaces the earlier one.
Replay stops at the first failure and leaves that write, and every write after it, queued.
On hydrate, a non-empty server list wins. A write still in the queue is applied on top, once, so it is not dropped and not duplicated.
An empty server name does not erase a name that exists only in the queue.
Pending reflections stay in front of the server list.

Do not add an API endpoint. The web client does not get this queue.

problem_statement:
A task lists the tasks it waits for in waitsFor.

Completing a waiting task is allowed, and the screen shows what it still waits for.
Refuse a self-link, a duplicate link, a link to a missing task, an eleventh prerequisite, and any link that would close a cycle.
A deleted or skipped prerequisite stops blocking. A finished task is never waiting.
The daily checklist skips tasks that are still waiting, and plans a waiting task for the day after its prerequisite is done.
Plan generation fills waitsFor from the template titles, and only when both tasks are in that plan. A short plan must not leave a task waiting for a title that was dropped.
If sync has already created a cycle, readers finish instead of looping.
The original pull request body is an empty template. This statement is the behavior the tests grade.

problem_statement:
Add account export and account deletion on the auth server.

Export requires a session. It returns that account and every wedding it belongs to, with records. It contains nothing secret and nothing from a wedding they are not in.
Delete requires the session and the password, and refuses anything else. Another person's password does nothing.
A shared wedding is handed to the partner. A solo wedding is deleted with its records.
After deletion, nothing still points at that account, every session ends, the email can be used again, and invites they sent stop working.
A partner who leaves loses only their part.
Password guesses are limited per account, including from a new address each time, and a stolen session cannot guess without that limit.

The graded file is server/auth/account.test.mjs. It uses node:sqlite and node:test. Do not add a new auth issuer.

problem_statement:
Guests reply on a page served by the API, and the phone's sync channel cannot write those replies.

A member can save the page settings. A taken slug is refused. Settings are members only.
Issuing a link returns the public URL and a readable code once. Reissuing or revoking turns the old link off.
The page shows only that invitation's guests, by first name, and escapes names that look like markup.
A made-up token is refused. A code works only on its own wedding. An unknown wedding page is a 404.
Replies stop after the deadline day. The link stops working 30 days after the deadline.
A reply is recorded without writing the guest records through this request, and a later reply can change the answer.
A meal that is not on the list is rejected.
Guessing codes is slowed per address and per wedding, across addresses.
Devices cannot write replies through sync. Guest pages work without the app token. The API still requires it.

Every interpolated value is escaped.

problem_statement:
After onboarding, Home must stay usable when today's reading fails.

A successful GET /today shows no failure banner.
A failed GET /today shows a retry and a real passage, and Reading still opens.
An empty /today payload is the same visible failure, and retry can recover.
A request that never returns still shows retry on a short frame.

Keep the error inside the tab. Do not leave the screen on an ellipsis and do not unmount the tab onto the blank background.
